definitions.gloss: grilled mutton dish of Hokkaido; Genghis Khan barbecue
definitions.explanation: Slices of mutton or lamb grilled with vegetables on a dome-shaped iron skillet and dipped in a soy-based sauce. The best-known local dish of Hokkaido, eaten at restaurants, at beer gardens, and outdoors.

notes:
Named after ジンギスカン, the Japanese form of Genghis Khan; the link to the Mongol ruler is a marketing legend rather than history. The dish itself dates from early twentieth-century Hokkaido, where sheep were raised for wool.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ジンギスカン⟦{鍋|なべ}→鍋：01038_nabe⟧: the dome-shaped skillet used for the dish (also the dish itself)
- ジンギスカン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to go out for jingisukan
- ⟦{生|なま}→生：03509_nama⟧ラム⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ジンギスカン: jingisukan made with fresh (unfrozen) lamb

CULTURAL NOTE:
The curved skillet lets the fat run down to the vegetables at the rim while the meat cooks on top. In Hokkaido, outdoor jingisukan at ⟦{花見|はなみ}→花見：01700_hanami⟧ or beer gardens is as ordinary as a barbecue elsewhere in Japan.
